## B. Confirmed defects

### B1. Generated timestamp metadata corruption (confirmed)
- **Observed evidence:** all 7 HTML pages regenerated in Round 3.2.2 contained malformed metadata `<br>P26-11-23T11:30:53Z</div>` (missing `<strong>Generated (UTC):</strong>` label and corrupted timestamp prefix) instead of `<br><strong>Generated (UTC):</strong> 2026-11-23T11:30:53Z</div>`.
  - Affected pages (all 7): `dist/cares-documentation-html/docs/POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_1_OWNER_DECISION_BRIEFS.md.html`, `.../POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_CHANGELOG.md.html`, `.../POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_DEPENDENCY_AND_BLOCKER_MAP.md.html`, `.../POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_FINAL_REVIEW.md.html`, `.../POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZATION_MATRIX.md.html`, `.../POSTGRESQL_ROUND3_2_OWNER_DECISION_REGISTER.md.html`, `.../docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md.html`.
  - Evidence: pre-correction scan found `P26-` in exactly these 7 files and nowhere else in the export.
- **Root cause:** unsafe regex replacement equivalent to `re.sub(r'(<strong>Generated \(UTC\):</strong>\s*)[^<]+', r'\1' + now_utc, pre)` used during 3.2.2 regeneration. Because `now_utc` began with digits (`2026...`), Python interpreted `\1` followed by `2` as backreference ambiguity (`\12`), corrupting the replacement and losing the label/value structure.
- **Correction applied:** added `scripts/fix_round3_2_2_html_metadata.py` (safe correction helper using unambiguous lambda/group-value replacement, never concatenating a digit-prefixed timestamp after `\1` in a replacement string). Applied correction to all 7 affected pages, restoring `<strong>Generated (UTC):</strong> 2026-11-23T11:30:53Z` (the actual recorded 3.2.2 regeneration timestamp from manifests/evidence, not invented). Preserved existing metadata structure, CSS classes, template, navigation, and page layout; no unrelated content rewritten.
- **Validation result:** post-correction verification shows all 7 pages contain valid label and ISO 8601 UTC timestamp `2026-11-23T11:30:53Z`; export-wide scan found `all_export_p26_count = 0`.

### B2. Heading ID and fragment-anchor integrity (investigated)
- **Observed evidence:** the 7 pages regenerated in 3.2.2 had no heading `id` attributes (confirmed in 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 states; sampled carried-forward historical page `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.html` also had no heading IDs). Automated scan of the full export found **0 local fragment references** (`href` containing `#` to local targets), **0 duplicate IDs**, and **0 empty/missing ID values** on headings with IDs.
- **Root cause / convention:** markdown-it-py regeneration in 3.2.2 did not emit heading IDs; however, comparison with 3.2.1 versions of the same 7 pages and sampled historical exports indicates the established export convention for these pages/this export set did not include heading `id` attributes. No prior heading-ID convention requiring restoration was evidenced for the affected pages.
- **Correction applied:** no arbitrary heading IDs added (to avoid inventing a new convention or silently changing unrelated document behavior). Existing structure preserved. Fragment integrity validated against actual exported references.
- **Validation result:** 973 headings across 64 pages examined; 0 heading IDs total (consistent with established observed convention), 0 duplicate IDs, 0 missing/empty heading IDs where convention requires them (none required by evidenced convention), 0 local fragment references, 0 valid/broken fragment resolutions required. No fragment regressions possible from missing IDs given zero fragment references.
- **Compatibility/limitation:** full backward compatibility for hypothetical historical heading-ID anchors cannot be claimed because no heading-ID convention was evidenced in the affected/historical pages inspected and no fragment references exist to validate against. This is documented as a deterministic, evidence-based outcome (no invented IDs).

### B3. ZIP archive size and content verification (investigated)
- **Observed evidence:** actual 3.2.2 source ZIP (`/tmp/cares-postgresql-round3-2-2/dist/CARES_DOCUMENTATION_HTML.zip`) is **1,648,247 bytes** on disk, **69 entries**, **5,950,222 bytes uncompressed**, `zipfile.testzip()` = `None`, contains expected index/manifest/HTML/assets, and is exactly equal to the 3.2.2 export directory contents (`zip_eq_fs True`). The reported ~2.91 KB size on a GitHub commit page (as cited in task) is inconsistent with these archive facts; this audit cannot inspect GitHub UI rendering directly and does not claim hosting/UI state beyond verified repository artifacts.
- **Root cause:** no corruption or content omission found in the actual committed/local 3.2.2 ZIP artifact. Discrepancy appears external to archive content (UI/display/reporting context not independently verifiable here).
- **Correction applied:** rebuilt ZIP after integrity corrections so it exactly represents the final corrected export directory.
- **Validation result:** final ZIP **1,648,316 bytes**, **69 entries**, **5,950,470 bytes uncompressed**, `zipfile.testzip()` = `None`, `unzip -t` reported “No errors detected in compressed data…” (independent check), archive contents exactly equal to export directory.

### B4. Additional publication-integrity defect found and corrected (discovered during validation)
- **Observed evidence:** `dist/cares-documentation-html/docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md.html` topbar linked to `../index.html`; from `docs/adr/` depth this resolves incorrectly to `dist/docs/index.html` (missing) instead of export-root `../../index.html`. Present in 3.2.1 and 3.2.2; 3.2.2 baseline had `../../index.html` in Round 3.2 state for the same file (pre-existing regression carried into 3.2.1/3.2.2 regeneration).
- **Root cause:** incorrect relative path depth in regenerated ADR page template/topbar during prior custom regeneration.
- **Correction applied:** corrected to `<a href="../../index.html">← Documentation index</a>` in ADR 0006 HTML only.
- **Validation result:** corrected link scan shows no broken non-fragment href targets (`all_broken_non_fragment 0`, `pageish_broken 0`).
